source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: When a substance is exposed to air or water, decide whether it must be stored away from one of them because of its reactivity.
node_labels: Matter: materials, particles, mixtures and change

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Sulfur must be stored under water because it catches fire when exposed to air.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Sodium can be stored under water to keep air away.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Storing sodium in kerosene makes it react vigorously with air and water.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Sulfur cannot burn in air because it does not react with water.

intelligence.enrichment: Sodium is a metal stored in kerosene because it reacts vigorously with oxygen and water and produces much heat. Phosphorus is stored in water because it catches fire when exposed to atmospheric air, while sulfur placed in water shows no reaction. The way a substance reacts with oxygen, air, or water determines the storage condition that prevents dangerous reaction. The learner correctly applies this rule: Sodium is a metal stored in kerosene because it reacts vigorously with oxygen and water and produces much heat. Phosphorus is stored in water because it catches fire when exposed to atmospheric air, while sulfur placed in water shows no reaction. All reactive substances need the same storage liquid; the liquid just keeps them covered.
